items.question: When should I consult a gynaecologist?
items.answer: You should consult a gynaecologist if you experience irregular periods, severe pelvic pain, unusual discharge, or as part of your routine annual wellness screening.

items.question: What are common symptoms of ovarian cysts?
items.answer: Common symptoms include pelvic pain during periods, abdominal bloating or swelling, and pain during intercourse.

items.question: What causes irregular periods?
items.answer: Irregular periods can be caused by hormonal imbalances, PMOS, thyroid disorders, extreme stress, or sudden weight fluctuations.

items.question: When should pelvic pain be checked?
items.answer: Pelvic pain that is severe, persistent, or interferes with your daily activities should be evaluated by a gynaecologist immediately.

items.question: When should heavy bleeding be evaluated?
items.answer: If you soak through one or more sanitary pads every hour for several consecutive hours, or experience periods lasting longer than 7 days, you should consult a doctor.

items.question: How often should women have a gynaecology check-up?
items.answer: It is recommended for women to visit a gynaecologist at least once a year for a routine preventive health screening.

items.question: Can PMOS cause irregular periods?
items.answer: Yes, Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PMOS) is one of the most common causes of irregular or missed menstrual cycles.

items.question: When should I consult a doctor about menopause symptoms?
items.answer: You should consult a specialist if severe hot flashes, mood swings, or night sweats start disrupting your daily sleep and quality of life.
